title: Grade 4 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — Termly Exam #18 (Term 3)

pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does Purushartha mean? (1 mark)
   A. A festival
   B. A river
   C. A prayer
   D. The goals of life

2. Every living being has what, according to Hindu belief? (1 mark)
   A. A scripture
   B. A festival
   C. An atma, a small part of the divine
   D. A temple

3. What does the Shibi story teach? (1 mark)
   A. Kings do not care
   B. Hawks always win
   C. Doves are bad
   D. A kind person protects the weak

4. What does Moksha mean? (1 mark)
   A. A song
   B. Freedom of the soul
   C. A meal
   D. A game

5. Which statement is true about kindness? (1 mark)
   A. It is only for rich people
   B. It is only for humans
   C. It includes animals and nature
   D. It is only for adults

6. What did King Shibi offer to save the dove? (1 mark)
   A. His own flesh, weight for weight
   B. His horse
   C. His crown
   D. His shoes

7. How many Purusharthas are there? (1 mark)
   A. Four
   B. Five
   C. Two
   D. Ten

8. Which king protected a dove in a well-known story? (1 mark)
   A. Harishchandra
   B. Hiranyakashipu
   C. King Shibi
   D. Ravan

9. Why is prayer a principle of Dharma? (1 mark)
   A. It ends homework
   B. It makes us proud
   C. It makes us thankful, calm and humble
   D. It builds houses

10. Which is a reason for celebrating festivals? (1 mark)
   A. To stop learning
   B. To avoid friends
   C. To remember important events and teachings
   D. To waste time

11. Which activity is suggested to learn about festivals? (1 mark)
   A. Watch television all day
   B. Copy a friend's essay
   C. Write a composition on your favourite festival
   D. Read a book quietly

12. Maha Shivratri means what? (1 mark)
   A. The day of forgiveness
   B. The great night of Shiva
   C. The festival of lights
   D. The great day of the Sun

13. What is Paryushan Parva mainly about? (1 mark)
   A. Racing
   B. Prayer, self-control and forgiveness
   C. Wealth
   D. Feasts only

14. What does charity work at festivals help with? (1 mark)
   A. Buying more sweets for ourselves
   B. Wasting food
   C. Making noise
   D. Sharing with those who cannot afford food or clothes

15. What does Micchami Dukkadam mean? (1 mark)
   A. May any harm I did be forgiven
   B. Good morning
   C. Happy birthday
   D. Thank you for the food

16. Which is the largest planet in the solar system? (1 mark)
   A. Venus
   B. Jupiter
   C. Mercury
   D. Mars

17. Which two heavenly bodies besides the five planets are counted as grahas? (1 mark)
   A. The stars and clouds
   B. Earth and Pluto
   C. The Sun and the Moon
   D. The Sun and Earth

18. Which planet is famous for its rings? (1 mark)
   A. Venus
   B. Saturn
   C. Mercury
   D. Mars

19. What is the Sun in modern science? (1 mark)
   A. A star
   B. A planet
   C. A moon
   D. A comet

20. Which day is linked with Saturn? (1 mark)
   A. Saturday
   B. Thursday
   C. Sunday
   D. Monday

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how to make a decorated calendar. (4 marks)

22. What is Dharma? (2 marks)

23. Explain the meaning of the word Paramatma. (2 marks)

24. Explain the meaning of karma. (3 marks)

25. Explain why balance is important in the four Purusharthas. (5 marks)

26. Distinguish between Madaraka Day and Jamhuri Day. (3 marks)

27. List the five principles of Dharma studied in the lesson. (2 marks)

28. Why should we visit a friend's festival respectfully? (3 marks)

29. Write the Indian names for Thursday and Friday. (2 marks)

30. On which date is Madaraka Day and what does Madaraka mean? (2 marks)

31. State two things people do on Maha Shivratri. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — The goals of life
   Purushartha means the goals of a person's life.

2. C — An atma, a small part of the divine
   This is why Hindus respect all life.

3. D — A kind person protects the weak
   Kindness protects the weak.

4. B — Freedom of the soul
   Moksha is the highest goal.

5. C — It includes animals and nature
   Kindness includes all living beings.

6. A — His own flesh, weight for weight
   He offered himself.

7. A — Four
   There are four.

8. C — King Shibi
   King Shibi saved the dove.

9. C — It makes us thankful, calm and humble
   Prayer helps us feel calm.

10. C — To remember important events and teachings
   Festivals help us remember.

11. C — Write a composition on your favourite festival
   Writing helps us reflect.

12. B — The great night of Shiva
   Maha means great and ratri means night.

13. B — Prayer, self-control and forgiveness
   These are its main themes.

14. D — Sharing with those who cannot afford food or clothes
   We share with the needy.

15. A — May any harm I did be forgiven
   It is a plea for forgiveness.

16. B — Jupiter
   Jupiter is the biggest.

17. C — The Sun and the Moon
   The seven days link to Sun, Moon and five planets.

18. B — Saturn
   Saturn has bright rings.

19. A — A star
   The Sun is a star.

20. A — Saturday
   Shanivaar.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw a table with seven columns, write English and Indian names, draw the Sun, Moon and planets above their days, and decorate it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: The right way of living, including duty, honesty and kindness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for two ideas.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Supreme Soul, or God.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Karma means action. Good actions bring good results and unkind actions bring trouble.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for action, 1 mark for good, 1 mark for unkind.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: Wealth and wishes are good but must follow Dharma. Without balance, chasing money or wishes can lead to cheating and harm, while Dharma keeps us honest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for balance, 2 marks for Dharma guiding the others, 2 marks for an example.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Madaraka Day is 1 June and marks internal self-government in 1963. Jamhuri Day is 12 December and marks independence in 1963 and the republic in 1964.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each date and 1 mark for a difference.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Paramatma, Purushartha, Prani Daya, Punarjanam, Prarthana (any correct set earns marks).
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each, rounded up.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: We listen, ask polite questions, do not laugh at customs, and build peace among communities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Thursday: Guruvaar. Friday: Shukravaar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: 1 June; power or authority to govern.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fast, stay awake all night, bathe the Shiva Linga, offer bel leaves, chant Om Namah Shivaya (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
